title: Elector Frederick William of Brandenburg and Count Georg Friedrich of Waldeck, Aug-Sept 1655 (catalogue 2539): letter-for-number substitution recovered from the clear passages and the ciphertext, checked against a summary decipherment of the time on scan 819; the Elector's four pieces and Waldeck's two letters share the key

steps.what: Scans 715-819 of the volume captured from the archieven.nl viewer in headless Chromium at device scale 2 (about 2490 x 3400 px), one page at a time (scripts/anl_view.py).

One web search in German (Kurfürst, Waldeck, Cöslin, September 1655, Woywoden, Krockow, Danzig, Weichsel) and the catalogue vetting of 11 Nov 2026: no edition, quotation or decipherment of these letters found. Erdmannsdörffer 1869 not opened.

Sign conventions written first; every cipher line transcribed in two passes from crops and reconciled on the image (12 lines changed in pass 2). The key became evident during pass 1 of scans 795 and 793, so pass 1 of the other scans and all of pass 2 were made with the key known.

In c793 the run after the clear words 'den von' (15.8.1.12.15.1.3.3) fits the name Krockow, known from an instruction dated Cöslin 4/14 Sept 1655; with e = 4 (the commonest number) and -en = 4.7 the common words gave the rest. Key frozen from c793 alone (key_frozen.tsv, 22 values).

Held-out test (scripts/heldout.py, heldout.txt): the frozen key's mechanical decryption of the 40 cipher groups of scan 819 matches 196 of the 209 letters of the margin decipherment of the time in order (0.938) and 30 of its 37 words letter for letter; the misses are the note's own wording and two writer's slips. The two glosses of scan 797 give letter ratios 0.83 and 0.77. In the other documents every number is in the frozen key except 18 and 51 (Waldeck's letters).

All four documents decrypted mechanically with key.tsv and read as German with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py rebuilds the decryptions and fails on any unmarked departure. Verbatim shares: c793 90.9%, ps797 93.8%, ps717 95.8%, l819 96.9%.

Independent review by an AI language-model agent: 15 cipher lines (about 190 numbers) copied from the scans before opening any transcription, all agreeing; mark check, frozen key and held-out test reproduced; reading review per document (ps717 and l819 grade A, c793 and ps797 grade B). It found a hole of 794.09 moved to the next line in the reading and asked for the clean-share source to be shipped.

Fixes after the review: 794.09-794.10 marked so the binding hole stays on its line (dr{[...]/ü}-); scripts/reading.py now also fails when a [...] or [nn] of the decryption is dropped from a reading without a mark; the sentence texts used for the clean share are shipped in work/. No count changed.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 2474 tokens, 26 types, de-1640s order 4: reading -2.245 per letter; random keys -6.617 (z 8.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -4.169 (mean -4.226, z 61.3); annealer on the real text -2.245. Verdict: pass.
Waldeck letters (w787, w813): Scans 787-789 and 813-814 captured from the archieven.nl viewer, as for targets/friedrichwilhelm1655.

Waldeck letters (w787, w813): The cipher passages and the clear words next to them transcribed in two passes from crops and reconciled; pass 2 was made with the key known. The clear text between the passages is not transcribed.

Waldeck letters (w787, w813): The key frozen from the Elector's letter c793 (targets/friedrichwilhelm1655) applied unchanged. These letters were not used to build it: every number in them is in the frozen key except 18 (x, from 'Weixel', added after the freeze) and 51 (twice).
Waldeck letters (w787, w813): Both letters decrypted mechanically and read as German with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py passes.

Waldeck letters (w787, w813): Independent review by an AI language-model agent: blind spot-check of cipher lines 813.a, 813.b, 787.a, 787.b, 814.05 and 814.07 (with nine lines of the Elector's letters) against the scans, all agreeing; mark check reproduced; reading review grade B for both letters. It found four line ends of 814 where a binding hole was dropped from the reading without a mark.

Waldeck letters (w787, w813): Fixes after the review: 814.05, 814.07, 814.08 and 814.10 marked {[...]/} (nothing is lost; the word runs on); w813 verbatim falls from 67 to 64 words, repairs rise from 2 to 5. scripts/reading.py now fails on any unmarked dropped hole. Sentence texts shipped in work/.

Integration check (12 Nov 2026), by a second AI language-model reader, not the contributor: all scripts re-run (heldout.txt, check_marks, decryptions identical); own decoder from key.tsv agrees on ps717 and l819 letter for letter; scans 819, 717, 795 and 813 fetched from the viewer and 111 groups (558 numbers) compared: l819 lines 4-15, ps717 lines 8-14, 795.06-795.14 and 813.a-c: one number and one clear word wrong (see the next step).

Corrections from the image check: 819.11 last group is 16.5.7.12 (c), not 16.5.7.13 (f), so the slip is 'lanctag' (12 for 11), not 'lanftag'; the clear word at 795.06 is 'auß', not 'auch' ('durch vorspan auß Pommern'; translation 'from Pomerania'). Held-out score unchanged (196/209). Decryptions rebuilt, check_marks passes.

Waldeck's folder (targets/waldeck1655, PR #471) folded into this one: one key, one entry. Outcome recomputed over the six documents with the strict rule (verbatim words only count as read): 704 of 760 words (92.6%), read in part; documents ps717 (95.8%) and l819 (96.9%) reach the bar. Method set to key recovered based on adjacent plaintext (the clear words of the same letter and the name Krockow gave the key, not ciphertext alone).

Integration: Erdmannsdörffer, Graf Georg Friedrich von Waldeck (1869), fetched as text from archive.org (grafgeorgfriedri00erdmuoft and bub_gb_-E06AAAAcAAJ, Fraktur OCR with long-s errors) and searched with OCR-tolerant patterns for Krockow, Cöslin, Radziwill, Danzig, Marienwerder, Culemborg and Chiffre/Ziffer: no hit; the OCR is too poor to exclude a quotation of the letters.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.245; polyphony 0.0; 2 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.245

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Simple substitution of letters by numbers; the key was found in c793 from the clear words around the runs and the name Krockow (an outside guess), frozen, then tested on the margin decipherment of scan 819 (196 of 209 letters in order, 0.938) and the two glosses of scan 797, and applied unchanged to Waldeck's two letters (51 has no value).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Six documents, words as counted by scripts/reading.py (clear words included): 704 of 760 verbatim; repairs, context fills and holes count as not read (strict README rule). Scans 723-724 (another code) not treated. The clear text of Waldeck's letters, scan 819 lines 1-3 and the clear opening lines of 793 are not cipher and are not transcribed in full.

texts.label: Cöslin, 4 Sept 1655, cipher body
texts.summary: The army will be on the Vistula within ten days and Waldeck's troops are to be there; ships ready in the Königsberg Haff; 24,000 lb of bread a day, as much beer, forage for 6,000 horses; Gerhard Roggen at Danzig and Christoph Melchior to help; the artillery pieces to be left behind but the horses brought; Danzig refuses passage, von Krockow sent to treat with the city and the voivodes.
texts.note: 286 words (about 104 of them clear), 260 verbatim (90.9%), 4 marked repairs, 21 context fills (letters lost in the binding of scan 794), 4 holes; checker clean share 0.70.

reading_review.note: The prose holds throughout; 21 context fills, mostly evident letters lost at the binding, and 4 holes. 'Nebro' is not identified, and the clear word at 795.06 was checked on the image at integration: 'auß', not 'auch'.

texts.label: P.S. of 4 Sept 1655
texts.summary: Send out fifty horsemen to find the Elector's march and report; small parties of five or six; build an entrenchment for about 500 foot on this side of the Vistula; ships ready to put the troops across if danger arises.
texts.note: 161 words (about 75 clear), 151 verbatim (93.8%), 3 repairs, 6 fills (binding of scan 798), 4 holes; clean share 0.765.

reading_review.note: The orders for patrols and the entrenchment read cleanly. The last two sentences (798.06-08) have 3 holes and are thin, and one clear word (797.20) is not read.

texts.label: Postscriptum, August 1655
texts.summary: Kept in suspense; treaties with the local people, especially the Weihers, to stay non-binding; proceed with Ermland; no other protection allowed; Elbing subject to ratification; tell the Oberräte with caution; the troops are marching.
texts.note: 71 words, 68 verbatim (95.8%), 3 marked repairs, no holes; clean share 0.714.

reading_review.note: 95.8% verbatim, 3 marked writer's slips, no holes; the sentences hold.

texts.label: September 1655, Radziwill passage
texts.summary: Radziwill gives to understand that they see no course but to place themselves under the Elector's protection; a general Prussian diet should be called by the Bishop of Ermland and the Elector should bring it about.
texts.note: 64 words, 62 verbatim (96.9%), 2 repairs, no holes; clean share 1.00. A summary decipherment of the time stands in the margin. Integration check: the last group of 819.11 is 12 (c), not 13; the slip reads lanctag.

reading_review.note: 96.9% verbatim; the summary decipherment of the time in the margin confirms it independently.

texts.label: 7 Sept 1655, six passages
texts.summary: Conditions with Sweden could hardly be worse; letters sent to Jacob Weiher, Elbing and Danzig; will speak to the Bishop of Ermland; Danzig offers ships; vivres against cartage money or security; news to General Sparr.
texts.note: Passages only. 106 words (about 63 clear), 99 verbatim (93.4%), 1 repair, 6 fills, 4 holes; clean share 0.889.

reading_review.note: Only the cipher passages are edited and the clear text between them is left out, so several passages are fragments; 788.20-24 has 4 holes.

texts.label: Königsberg, 14 Sept 1655
texts.summary: Weiher offers help; Vistula boats ordered at Marienwerder; Magnus reports that Thorn resolves to defend itself and plans a meeting with Danzig, Elbing and the three voivodes on the Vistula, and is not unwilling to help [51].
texts.note: 72 words, 64 verbatim (88.9%), 5 marked repairs (four of them line ends in the binding where nothing is lost, marked {[...]/}), 3 fills, 2 holes ([51] twice); checker clean share 0.833 on the sentence text.

reading_review.note: The sentences hold. [51] (twice) is unresolved; reading it as the Elector is a guess.

gaps.detail: One name with no context to identify it; read from the signs.

gaps.item: Erdmannsdörffer, Graf Georg Friedrich von Waldeck (1869)
gaps.detail: Named in the catalogue's verify field. Searched at integration in the two online Fraktur OCR copies (archive.org): no hit for Krockow, Cöslin, Radziwill, Danzig, Marienwerder, Culemborg or Chiffre, but the OCR is too poor to exclude a quotation; the book draws on the Arolsen archive.
Not a letter; from context a person, perhaps the Elector. Reading it as the Elector is a guess.
Four holes; letters lost in the binding.
2 or 12 not settled on the image.
One name in Waldeck's letter, not identified.
A different code (numbers up to four digits mixed with letters); no key of this code is known; not treated here, so catalogue item 2539 stays open for it.

prior.where: Scan 819 carries a summary decipherment of its cipher in the left margin, in another hand of the time, and scan 797 two interlinear glosses (so bald, zu dero). Both were held out and not used to build the key. No edition or modern decipherment found: one web search (12 Nov 2026); catalogue vetting of 11 Nov 2026 (Urkunden und Actenstücke VII opened, the Cöslin letter is not printed; DECODE and Cryptiana have nothing). Erdmannsdörffer, Graf Georg Friedrich von Waldeck (1869): not opened by the contributor; searched at integration in two online Fraktur OCR copies with no hit, but the OCR is too poor to exclude a quotation. The catalogue entry of 11 Nov 2026 already said that scan 819 'may be a contemporary decipherment (not read)', so the note was known to exist before the work; that it was not used for the key rests on the contributor's record (one commit per PR, no external timestamp). Waldeck's register copies carry marginal summaries of the clear text only.

human: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 2539) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, recovered and froze the key, applied it to Waldeck's two letters, ran the held-out test, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
